purpose: Backup original content of 17 news_articles rows before removing metadata from reading and translation

rows.title: Biodegradable tampons
rows.content:
Plastic period products are bad for the natural world. They are the fifth most common plastic on European beaches. There are more of them than plastic cups and straws.

The European Parliament wants to find better options. They are looking into using biodegradable materials, like fibers from algae, to make tampons.

These tampons are from a white material. So it is not necessary to make them white with chemicals. It is important to grow these materials in a way which does not hurt the natural world. Researchers are working on better ways to do this on land and in the sea. We need to throw away less plastics.

Ảnh minh họa sản phẩm vệ sinh: Editingob / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0.

rows.title: How Donald Trump makes money
rows.content:
US President Donald Trump made more than 1.4 billion dollars from digital currency projects in 2025. A new official financial report shows that most of his income now comes from these digital assets.

Trump and his sons started a crypto project called World Liberty Financial, which earned nearly 800 million. This money came from selling digital tokens and business shares. Trump also made 635 million from a special digital coin named after him. Since he returned to the White House, his family earned around 2.3 billion from digital money.

A spokesperson said there is no problem with his official work and business. At the same time, Trump’s businesses, like his golf clubs and beautiful resorts, did very well and brought in more than 500 million last year.

Ảnh chân dung: Daniel Torok / White House, Wikimedia Commons · Public domain.

rows.title: To buy or to rent? – level 1
rows.content:
Two sisters, Morgan and Lisa, live in similar houses. They are part of an example that compares buying a home with renting one. Morgan buys her house with help from a bank. Lisa rents a house and pays its owner every month.

When something breaks, Morgan must pay for repairs. Lisa usually asks the owner to fix problems. After many years, Morgan may fully own her home. Lisa can move more easily and can save or invest money instead.

In this example, both women spend money over thirty years, but in different ways. Buying can help a person build wealth. Renting can offer more freedom. The better choice depends on the home price, savings and future plans.

Sources: News in Levels. Article rewritten for English learners; original illustration by LDD English.

Ảnh minh họa nhà rao bán: Jidanni / Wikimedia Commons · CC0 1.0.

rows.title: A politician is hurt in Australia – level 1
rows.content:
Helen Haines is a politician in Australia. On October 19, a car hit her outside her office in the town of Wangaratta. Police believe the driver hit her on purpose. People nearby helped stop the driver, and police arrested a man.

Haines was badly injured. Doctors had to remove both of her legs. On October 24, the hospital said that her condition had improved. She was still seriously hurt, but she was stable.

People across Australia sent flowers and kind messages. Leaders spoke about keeping public workers safe. Police are still investigating the reason for the attack.

Sources: News in Levels and ABC News (24 October update). Article rewritten for English learners; original illustration by LDD English.

Ảnh chân dung Helen Haines năm 2022: Alison Newman / Wikimedia Commons · CC0 1.0.

rows.title: Young people and concussion – level 1
rows.content:
Children sometimes hurt their heads when they play football and other sports. A head injury called a concussion can cause a headache, tiredness or trouble thinking clearly.

In the past, people often believed that children needed a very long rest. Today, doctors usually advise a short rest, followed by a careful return to school and normal activities. Some students may need more breaks or extra help with schoolwork.

Parents should speak with a healthcare professional and watch how their child feels. Children must not return to contact sports until a medical professional says it is safe. Sleep, gentle walks and support from teachers can help children recover.

Sources: News in Levels and CDC guidance. Article rewritten for English learners; original illustration by LDD English.

Ảnh minh họa: Francis ackson soko / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0.

rows.title: The business of Roman Abramovich – level 1
rows.content:
Roman Abramovich is a rich businessman from Russia. He once owned Chelsea Football Club in England. A new report looks at how some companies managed his money and expensive property.

Reporters say that some advisers may have changed dates on business papers. The papers may have helped companies hide property and pay less tax. The property includes large boats and planes. Police in Cyprus are now studying these claims.

Abramovich says he has done nothing wrong. The police investigation is not finished. The report has started new questions about how large companies keep financial records.

Sources: News in Levels and The Guardian (22 October update). Article rewritten for English learners; original illustration by LDD English.

Ảnh Roman Abramovich năm 2019: Amir Hosseini / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 4.0.

rows.title: India’s big river project – level 1
rows.content:
India wants to connect two rivers, called the Ken and the Betwa. The plan includes a very large dam. The government hopes to send more water to dry areas and help people who grow food.

However, some families near the project are worried. Rising water has reached homes, fields and a temple. Some people say that the money offered to them is not enough for moving to a new home. Villagers have protested.

Nature groups are worried, too. The project could harm forests and the animals living there, including tigers. The government says the water is important for the region. Local people want fair help and protection for their land.

Sources: News in Levels and Reuters. Article rewritten for English learners; original illustration by LDD English.

Ảnh minh họa một đập tại Ấn Độ: Chidambara / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0.

rows.title: No more horses in New York streets – level 1
rows.content:
People visit Central Park in New York and sometimes ride in a carriage pulled by a horse. These rides are a long tradition, but many people worry about the animals on busy city roads.

In October 2026, New York City leaders voted to end horse-drawn carriage rides. Supporters of the change say that traffic, noise and hot weather can make life hard for horses. They want the city to use other kinds of rides for visitors.

Some carriage drivers are worried about losing their jobs. The city now needs to plan how the change will happen and how to help workers and horses. The plan aims to end these rides by 2028.

Ảnh minh họa: Colin W / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.

rows.title: Questions about Starlink in Ukraine – level 1
rows.content:
Ukraine uses Starlink to connect to the internet during the war with Russia. The service works through satellites in space, so it can help people communicate when other networks stop working.

A new report has raised questions about how the service is controlled. It says that some Starlink connections became slower during important moments in the war. These are reported claims, and people want to know more about what happened.

Some American politicians say that a service this important should have clear rules. They want reliable communication for people who depend on it. Ukraine and its partners are looking for ways to keep internet connections working during the war.

Ảnh minh họa: Odapresste / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

rows.title: A village for women in Syria – level 1
rows.content:
Jinwar is a village in the northeast of Syria. It was built as a place where women and children could live in a safer community. Some families came there after difficult experiences during the war.

The village has small homes, a school, places to learn new skills and a bakery. Women work together, grow food and help take care of the community. They make decisions about daily life and support one another.

Life in the region is not always easy. Still, many people in Jinwar say that having a home and a chance to work gives them hope. The village shows how neighbours can help each other build a new life.

Ảnh minh họa một làng khác ở Al-Hasakah, Syria: haitham alfalah / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0.

rows.title: Fake concert tickets in Canada – level 1
rows.content:
Many music fans wanted to see Taylor Swift perform in Toronto, Canada. Some parents bought tickets as gifts for their children. They were excited about going to the concert.

But more than one hundred people learned that the tickets they bought were not real. A Canadian couple was accused of taking about 265,000 dollars through fake ticket sales. Many fans lost money and could not enter the show.

The couple appeared in court. The people who lost money want a fair decision. This story reminds concert fans to check the seller and use trusted ticket websites before paying.

Ảnh minh họa vé hòa nhạc: Amanda Jean Thomas / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 2.0.

rows.title: Malaysian durians attract more buyers – level 1
rows.content:
Durian is a large fruit with a strong smell. Many people in Malaysia enjoy eating it. The country also wants more people in other places to try its durians, especially customers in China.

Farmers often let Malaysian durians become ripe on the tree. The fruit can then fall naturally to the ground. Many buyers like the taste, but a ripe durian does not stay fresh for long. This makes it hard to send the fruit far away.

Shops make durian cakes and ice cream, and some tourists travel to taste the fruit. Businesses hope that better transport and growing interest will help farmers sell more durians.

Ảnh minh họa: Dcubillas / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.

rows.title: 2026 Chemistry Nobel Prize – level 1
rows.content:
A chemistry story in 2026 focuses on how molecules can have different shapes. Two forms may look like a person's left and right hands.

The shapes can affect how a substance works in the body. This is important when researchers develop medicine and try to reduce harmful effects.

Scientists study these differences to understand chemical reactions and to design safer treatments.

Difficult words: molecule (a small group of atoms); shape (the form of something); researcher (a person who studies a subject); treatment (care used to help someone who is ill).

Ảnh minh họa phòng thí nghiệm: Rhoda Baer / National Cancer Institute / Wikimedia Commons · Public domain.

rows.title: Lithuania and nuclear weapons – level 1
rows.content:
Lithuania is discussing its rules about nuclear weapons and national safety. The country is close to Russia and Belarus.

Some political leaders want stronger cooperation with military partners. Other people fear that changing the rules could increase problems between neighbouring countries.

The discussions show how important questions about security have become in this part of Europe.

Difficult words: nuclear (related to energy from atoms); security (protection against danger); military (related to soldiers); cooperation (working together).

Ảnh minh họa tòa nhà quốc hội Lithuania: Mojmir Churavy / Wikimedia Commons · CC0 1.0.

rows.title: Indonesia’s vice president and school records – level 1
rows.content:
A court case in Indonesia has raised questions about the education records of Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka. Some people asked whether his documents met the rules for holding office.

Judges ended the case for procedural reasons. The decision did not settle every question raised in public about the records.

The story shows why official documents and clear election requirements are important.

Difficult words: vice president (a leader below the president); record (a document containing information); court (a place where judges decide cases); requirement (something that is necessary).

Ảnh Gibran Rakabuming Raka năm 2023: AntaraTV / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 3.0.

rows.title: Questions after a laboratory death in Russia – level 1
rows.content:
News of a laboratory worker's death in Siberia worried some people. There was concern about a possible infection, but the cause was not confirmed in the report.

Officials told residents to stay calm. Health experts said that one unexplained death does not prove that a wider disease outbreak has begun.

Clear medical tests and reliable information are important when people are worried about their health.

Difficult words: laboratory (a place for scientific experiments); infection (an illness caused by germs); outbreak (a sudden rise in illness cases); reliable (able to be trusted).

Ảnh minh họa phòng thí nghiệm: Diane A. Reid / NIH / Wikimedia Commons · Public domain.

rows.title: Gen Z and money – level 1
rows.content:
Many young adults have trouble saving money for their future. The cost of housing and daily life has increased in many places.

Pictures of wealthy people on social media can make young adults feel more pressure. Some wonder whether they will be able to buy a home or start a family.

People are learning to plan their spending, look for better opportunities and speak about the cost of living.

Difficult words: housing (homes and places to live); income (money that someone earns); pressure (worry caused by difficulties); budget (a plan for spending money).

Ảnh minh họa tiết kiệm: 401(K) 2012 / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 2.0.
